payload.body: Audio-dithering is a human-made signal processing technique that adds low-level noise to a digital audio signal before quantization or bit-depth reduction to decorrelate quantization error and prevent distortion artifacts. Parameters: dither noise shape (triangular, rectangular, Gaussian), amplitude relative to least significant bit, noise bandwidth, and application point in the processing chain. Persistence mechanism: documented in digital audio engineering literature, implemented in DAW plugins and audio hardware, and taught in audio engineering curricula; the technique persists through code libraries, plugin implementations, and standardized digital audio workflows. [formal: dithering audio | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.08]
